title: Avalon Tech - LLM porting and infra compatibility scoping
summary: Discovery call for porting Avalon Tech's stack from hosted OpenAI + on-prem vLLM/TGI to a hybrid Redwood deployment. Main concerns: eval parity, latency vs cost tradeoffs, private deployment (VPC/KMS), function-calling and embeddings compatibility, and performance benchmarks. Agreed next steps: Redwood to share security/compliance pack and preliminary benchmark plan; schedule technical deep dive with infra team week of Jan 6.
next_steps: Redwood - send security & SOC2 + private deployment docs (Maya) - due 2026-01-05
Schedule SE deep technical session with Avalon infra (Jonah) - propose slots for week of 2026-01-06
Share initial benchmark plan + sample workloads (Jonah) - due 2026-01-09
Avalon to share representative prompt set and cost targets (Priya) - due 2026-01-07
action_items: Maya - attach SOC 2 and ISO summaries + Redwood Private architecture diagram - 2026-01-05
Jonah - draft benchmark plan (latency/cost/throughput) and list of required infra for POC - 2026-01-09
Priya - upload 3 canonical prompt suites and current OpenAI usage CSV - 2026-01-07
Mark - provide access window for on-prem traffic capture / load test - 2026-01-08
transcript:
[00:00] Maya (Redwood AE): Hey everyone, thanks for taking the time. Quick roll call?
[00:06] Priya (Avalon): Hi, Priya here.
[00:08] Mark (Avalon): Mark on the call.
[00:09] Kevin (Avalon): Kevin, CTO.
[00:11] Jonah (Redwood SE): Jonah from Redwood, hi.
[00:14] Maya: Cool. Quick agenda — understand your current stack, main pain points, and see what migration path makes sense (hosted vs dedicated vs private).
[00:23] Priya: Great. To summarize where we are — we run a hybrid model. For high-sensitivity data we use an on-prem vLLM cluster (we call it v-LLM pods) for fine-tuned models, for general assistant features we use OpenAI completions. We're evaluating consolidation because managing two paths is expensive and brittle.
[00:38] Kevin: Yeah, the ops overhead is getting to us and the egress costs are high. Also we have some compliance folks asking for better auditability.
[00:44] Maya: Makes sense. When you say vLLM, is that the open-source vllm project or a vendor-managed install?
[00:50] Mark: It's mostly the open-source vllm running on our DGX fleet, packaged with some TGI shims. We've made a few local kernel patches for memory.
[00:57] Jonah: ok, so likely similar challenges others have had — kernel/quantization differences, tokenization mismatch, and chat/function-calling semantics.
[01:05] Priya: One big concern — eval parity. We get different outputs between OpenAI and our on-prem models, and we need to ensure Redwood won't make that worse. How do you approach parity?
[01:14] Jonah: good question. We run pairwise evals across model variants — side-by-side scoring with your prompt suite. There's usually three buckets: exact parity, acceptable degradation (semantic parity), and regression. For the POC we recommend using the same tokenizer and model family where possible, and we instrument regen/temperature controls.
[01:29] Kevin: Are there cases where tokenization differences cause hard breakages? We do a lot of token-sensitive prompts, so subtle shifts cause scoring drift.
[01:37] Jonah: yes — tokenization plus byte-pair encoding variance can change prompt length and padding behavior. We normally map to a target model variant in Redwood that matches the tokenizer byte-spec; for cases where models differ we add a normalization layer in pre-processing. It's not magic though, some tasks will need re-tuning.
[01:51] Priya: And function-calling — we use OpenAI's function call API heavily. Will Redwood hosted endpoints accept the same schema and semantics?
[01:58] Maya: Redwood API supports structured output and function-style tool calls, but there are implementation differences depending on the model runtime. For hosted we emulate the OpenAI style at the API layer; for private/dedicated, the runtime must support streaming structured signals. Jonah can talk about specific mapping.
[02:10] Jonah: right. For TGI/vLLM we sometimes need a shim that translates the LLM output into the OpenAI function payload; this is part of the POC work. It adds a few ms overhead but it's predictable.
[02:21] Mark: Ok. On security: we need SSO (SAML), customer-managed KMS, audit logs, and data residency for EU. How mature are Redwood Private features?
[02:31] Maya: Redwood Private supports VPC/private control plane, KMS integrations, and detailed audit logs. We have SOC2 and ISO summaries — I'll share them after. SSO is supported; for SAML we can do an IdP integration during onboarding.
[02:41] Kevin: Are audit logs real-time? Our compliance folks want immutable logs with export.
[02:45] Jonah: We persist request/response hashes, user tokens, and routing metadata to an append-only store and can export via S3 connectors or SIEM. For private deployments that remains customer-managed retention.
[02:55] Priya: Another angle — cost. We have a hard target to reduce token spend by 30% while keeping latency under 250ms p95 for short assistant queries. Is that realistic?
[03:05] Maya: Depends on workload mix and batching. Hosted uses automatic batching and caching; dedicated or private gives you more predictable throughput and cost. Redwood Optimize will recommend quantization and batching settings — Jonah can propose configurations.
[03:15] Jonah: For 250ms p95 you'd want a smaller served model or an optimized kernel path; if you're doing longer context or few-shot prompts that changes. We can pre-warm KV-caches and use prefix caching to cut token costs. Doing a short benchmark will give realistic numbers.
[03:30] Sofia (PM): We also use embeddings for semantic search. Any differences in embedding vectors across providers? We've seen drift between OpenAI and our own embeddings.
[03:39] Jonah: embeddings differ across model families; you can get different vector norms and similarity distributions. Redwood supports model-versioned embeddings and we can compute alignment transforms as part of migration — a small linear transform often helps.
[03:49] Priya: What about model compatibility for custom fine-tunes? We fine-tuned Llama-based models; will Redwood allow us to bring our checkpoints?
[03:57] Maya: Private/dedicated can host customer models; we have onboarding paths for customer artifacts and a vetting process. There are licensing considerations for some model weights; we can walk through that.
[04:08] Kevin: Latency for fine-tuned models — do you compile kernels or use quantized runtimes?
[04:12] Jonah: we have a compilation layer that picks optimized kernels based on sequence length and hardware. For quantized models we test 4-bit paths; latency varies by GPU and model, but you can usually gain 2-3x throughput with small quality tradeoffs. We'll show numbers in the POC.
[04:27] Mark: For the POC, we want to run three scenarios: 1) drop-in hosted replacement for OpenAI with zero code changes, 2) dedicated pool for consistent SLA, 3) private VPC with on-prem gateway and KMS. Is that feasible?
[04:40] Maya: yes that's a good scope. For scenario 1, we'll validate API-surface parity; scenario 2 will measure throughput/latency stability; scenario 3 will prove security and network integration.
[04:50] Priya: Timeframe — we want to decide vendor by end of Q1. We can run a 4-week POC starting mid-Jan.
[04:57] Maya: That aligns — we can schedule the SE deep dive first week of Jan and land the POC plan by Jan 9.
[05:02] Jonah: quick note on edge cases — you mentioned TGI shims and local kernel patches. We should capture the exact runtime differences (CUDA versions, custom ops) so we can reproduce perf.
[05:12] Mark: We'll extract the runtime list and a small repro bundle.
[05:14] Priya: Also, about rollback and graceful degradation — if a dedicated pool fails do you have automatic fallback to hosted? We need to ensure no downtime for high priority flows.
[05:23] Maya: yes — Redwood supports routing policies with fallback. You can set priority: dedicated -> hosted -> reduced-model fallback; we can configure costs and SLOs accordingly.
[05:32] Kevin: Any details on pricing models for dedicated vs private? We need ballpark numbers for budgeting.
[05:37] Maya: I'll send a pricing summary but ballpark: dedicated has reserved capacity pricing with a monthly commitment; private has a platform fee plus support and infra. Exact depends on GPUs and commitment term.
[05:48] Priya: last thing — data purge and retention. Our legal team requires 30-day minimum deletion and ability to audit deletes.
[05:56] Jonah: retention policies are configurable per-tenant; for private deployments it's customer-managed. We capture deletion logs in the audit trail.
[06:03] Maya: ok let's do a quick recap of next steps.
[06:06] Priya: go ahead.
[06:07] Maya: Redwood will: share SOC2/ISO summaries and private deployment architecture (Maya), draft benchmark plan and propose SE deep dive slots (Jonah). Avalon will share prompt sets, cost targets, and runbook for the on-prem runtime (Priya/Mark). We'll target the POC kickoff mid-Jan.
[06:25] Kevin: sounds good.
[06:26] Maya: thanks everyone, we'll follow up via email with calendar invites and the docs.
[06:30] Priya: thanks.
[06:31] Maya: Bye.
notes: Customer emphasized eval parity and tokenization drift; uses vLLM + TGI on-prem plus OpenAI hosted. Agreed three-scenario POC (hosted drop-in, dedicated, private VPC). Security requirements (SAML, KMS, audit) are blockers without docs. POC to include benchmark on latency and embedding alignment.
